decisions.title: Browser interaction annotation
decisions.detail: Every browser interaction action within a research session records: action_type, target_selector (if applicable), timestamp_ms, and optional screenshot_ref.

decisions.title: Code-block copy visibility
decisions.detail: Always-visible copy affordance on fenced code blocks. Not hover/focus gated. Copy is NOT available on search result cards or diff cards.

decisions.title: /skill discovery paths

decisions.title: Task lifecycle states
decisions.detail: 6-state lifecycle: pending → queued → running → success | failed | cancelled. Failure: 3 retries with exponential backoff (1s, 4s, 16s). Timeout: per-task default 300s, configurable. Cancel: graceful (SIGTERM, 5s grace, SIGKILL).

decisions.title: Batch timeout formula
decisions.detail: `individual_timeout × min(url_count, 5)`, cap 600s. Applies to both batch webfetch and batch webextract.

The canonical web tool family comprises six operations. Each is a first-class built-in tool with its own permission key, provider routing, and audit surface.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

#### Canonical web operations

| Tool | Permission key | Primary purpose | Default | Mutation | Batch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `websearch` | `websearch` | Keyword/semantic web search | `ask` | No | No |
| `webfetch` | `webfetch` | Retrieve + render a URL | `ask` | No | Yes (max 50) |
| `webextract` | `webextract` | Structured extraction from a URL | `ask` | No | Yes (max 10) |
| `webresearch` | `webresearch` | Multi-step research workflow | `ask` | No | No |
| `webcrawl` | `webcrawl` | Recursive site crawl | `ask` | No | No |
| `webmap` | `webmap` | Site structure / sitemap discovery | `ask` | No | No |

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

#### Cross-cutting rules

- `Reading Site` remains the PM-native Site Reader path rather than a provider-local synonym.
- Provider support is disclosed as `native`, `pm_composed`, or `unsupported` per the capability matrix below.
- Natural-language requests and `/web` subcommands route to the same dispatcher.
- Provider fallback and evidence provenance remain visible in activity/audit surfaces.
- All web tools emit a `tool.web.*` seglog event family with the web audit payload (see `Plans/storage-plan.md` §4.4).
- Web tool errors use PM's 12-code error taxonomy; provider-specific codes are mapped (see Firecrawl error mapping below).

#### `websearch` contract

**Parameters:**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `string` | Yes | — | Search query text |
| `max_results` | `integer` | No | 10 | Maximum results to return (1–50) |
| `sources` | `string[]` | No | `["web"]` | Source types: `web`, `news`, `images`, `code`, `academic` |
| `categories` | `string[]` | No | `[]` | Optional filter: `github`, `research`, `pdf` |
| `region` | `string` | No | `"auto"` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or `"auto"` |
| `time_range` | `string` | No | `"any"` | `any`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year` |

**Output:** `{ results: Array<{ title, url, snippet, source_type, published_date? }>, provider_id, cache_state, search_metadata }`.

**Errors:** `invalid_query`, `provider_unavailable`, `rate_limited`, `timeout`.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

#### `webfetch` contract

**Parameters:**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | Yes | — | URL to fetch |
| `formats` | `string[]` | No | `["markdown"]` | Output formats: `markdown`, `html`, `rawHtml`, `screenshot`, `pdf`, `summary`, `links`, `images` |
| `actions` | `WebAction[]` | No | `[]` | Browser actions to execute before extraction (max 10, total wait max 30s) |
| `max_content_length` | `integer` | No | 5242880 | Max response size in bytes (default 5 MB) |
| `cache_policy` | `object` | No | `{max_age_seconds: 14400, store: true}` | Cache behavior override |
| `change_tracking` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Enable hash-based change detection vs prior fetch |
| `pdf_mode` | `string` | No | `"auto"` | PDF extraction mode: `fast`, `auto`, `ocr` |
| `timeout_ms` | `integer` | No | 30000 | Per-URL timeout |

**Output:** `{ content: Record<format, string|binary_ref>, metadata: { title, description, language, status_code, content_type }, cache_state: "hit"|"miss"|"stale"|"bypass", change_status?: "new"|"same"|"changed"|"removed", change_diff?: string, provider_id }`.

**Errors:** `invalid_url`, `fetch_failed`, `timeout`, `content_too_large`, `blocked_by_robots`, `ssl_error`, `dns_error`, `provider_unavailable`, `rate_limited`.

**Screenshot/PDF format note:** `screenshot` and `pdf` formats require browser runtime and elevate to `session_granted` permission tier.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

#### `webextract` contract

**Parameters:**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | Yes | — | URL to extract from |
| `schema` | `object` | No | `{}` | JSON Schema (draft-07) defining desired output shape. Max 50 KB. No external `$id` references. |
| `schema_mode` | `string` | No | `"lenient"` | `strict` (hard validation) or `lenient` (best-effort) |
| `prompt` | `string` | No | `""` | Natural-language extraction guidance (max 2000 chars). Prompt guides extraction; schema validates output. |
| `actions` | `WebAction[]` | No | `[]` | Browser actions before extraction |
| `formats` | `string[]` | No | `["markdown"]` | Intermediate fetch format |
| `timeout_ms` | `integer` | No | 30000 | Per-URL timeout |

**Output:** `{ extracted: object, raw_content?: string, schema_validation: { valid: boolean, errors?: string[] }, provider_id, cache_state }`.

**Empty extraction:** If no data matches the schema, return `{ extracted: {}, schema_validation: { valid: false, errors: ["no_matching_data"] } }` rather than fabricating content.

**Errors:** `invalid_url`, `invalid_schema`, `extraction_failed`, `timeout`, `provider_unavailable`, `rate_limited`.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

#### `webresearch` contract

**Parameters:**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `string` | Yes | — | Research question |
| `max_sources` | `integer` | No | 5 | Maximum sources to consult (1–20) |
| `starting_urls` | `string[]` | No | `[]` | Seed URLs (max 5) |
| `autonomous` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Enable multi-step autonomous mode |
| `depth` | `string` | No | `"standard"` | `quick` (1 search), `standard` (1–2 searches + reads), `deep` (up to 3 iterations) |
| `output_format` | `string` | No | `"report"` | `report`, `bullets`, `table` |
| `timeout_ms` | `integer` | No | 120000 | Total research timeout |

**Autonomous mode tiers:**
1. **PM-composed (default):** PM orchestrates search → fetch → synthesize pipeline. No provider-native agent.
2. **Enhanced PM-composed:** PM runs up to 3 search iterations, reads up to `max_sources` pages, refines query between iterations. Max 120s.
3. **Provider-native agent:** Delegates to provider's agent endpoint (e.g., Firecrawl `/agent`). Requires explicit user confirmation when estimated cost exceeds 100 credits. Hard cap default 500 credits (user-adjustable).

**Autonomous bounds:** Max 3 search iterations, max `max_sources` reads, max 120s total.

**Output:** `{ report: string, sources: Array<{ url, title, relevance_score, snippets_used }>, methodology: string, iterations_used: integer, provider_id, cost_credits?: number }`.

**Partial results on budget exceeded:** If autonomous mode hits credit cap, return partial results gathered so far with `truncation_reason: "credit_cap_exceeded"`.

**Errors:** `invalid_query`, `no_results`, `timeout`, `credit_cap_exceeded`, `provider_unavailable`, `rate_limited`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `max_pages` | `integer` | No | 10 | Maximum pages to crawl (1–100) |
| `max_depth` | `integer` | No | 3 | Maximum link-follow depth |
| `include_paths` | `string[]` | No | `[]` | Glob-style path inclusion filters (applied first) |
| `exclude_paths` | `string[]` | No | `[]` | Glob-style path exclusion filters (applied after include) |
| `formats` | `string[]` | No | `["markdown"]` | Output format per page |

**Async model:** Crawls exceeding 30s or 20 pages use async job polling: `{ job_id, status: "queued"|"running"|"complete"|"failed", progress: { pages_done, pages_total } }`.

#### `WebAction` type definition

A `WebAction` is a browser interaction step executed within a page context before content extraction.

```
WebAction = {
  type: "click" | "type" | "scroll" | "wait" | "screenshot" | "select" | "hover" | "evaluate" | "press" | "focus",
  selector?: string,        // CSS selector for target element
  value?: string,           // Text to type, key to press, or JS to evaluate
  timeout_ms?: integer,     // Max wait for this action (default 5000)
  description?: string      // Human-readable annotation for audit
}
```

**Constraints:** Max 10 actions per invocation. Total wait across all actions max 30s. `evaluate` actions are sandboxed — no access to PM internals.

#### Async progress model (long-running operations)

Operations that exceed 30s or trigger async backend processing (webcrawl, long webresearch) return a job handle:

```
AsyncJobHandle = {
  job_id: string,
  status: "queued" | "running" | "complete" | "failed",
  progress?: { done: integer, total: integer, current_url?: string },
  estimated_completion_ms?: integer,
  result_ref?: string   // set when status = "complete"
}
```

The agent polls via the same tool name with `{ job_id }` as the sole parameter. Poll interval: recommended 2s, backoff to 5s after 10 polls.

## 10. Firecrawl provider integration

Firecrawl is a web scraping and crawling API that PM integrates as a lower-priority provider in the web tool routing chain.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

### 10.1 Provider identity

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `provider_id` | `firecrawl` |
| Default state | Disabled — requires API key or self-hosted URL |
| Config location | Global user settings |
| Priority | Below Exa, Tavily; above DDG (user-adjustable) |
| Transport | HTTPS REST API (cloud) or user-provided base URL (self-hosted) |

### 10.2 Capability support

Firecrawl supports all 6 PM web operations natively:

| PM operation | Firecrawl endpoint | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| `websearch` | `/search` (uses Serper/Google) | `native` |
| `webfetch` | `/scrape` | `native` |
| `webextract` | `/scrape` with extract config | `native` |
| `webresearch` | `/agent` | `native` |
| `webcrawl` | `/crawl` | `native` |
| `webmap` | `/map` | `native` |

**Important:** Firecrawl search uses Serper (Google keyword search) while Exa uses semantic search — these produce fundamentally different result profiles. PM should not treat them as interchangeable.

### 10.3 Parameter mapping (PM → Firecrawl)

#### websearch → `/search`

| PM param | Firecrawl param | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | `query` | Direct |
| `max_results` | `limit` | Capped at Firecrawl's max |
| `region` | `lang` / `country` | Mapped from ISO 3166-1 |
| `time_range` | `tbs` | Mapped to Google time param |

#### webfetch → `/scrape`

| PM param | Firecrawl param | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `url` | Direct |
| `formats` | `formats` | `markdown` → `markdown`, `html` → `html`, `screenshot` → `screenshot`, `links` → `links` |
| `actions` | `actions` | Direct mapping; PM `WebAction` types map 1:1 to Firecrawl action types |
| `timeout_ms` | `timeout` | Converted to seconds |
| `cache_policy` | — | PM-side only; Firecrawl has no cache API |

#### webextract → `/scrape` with extract

| PM param | Firecrawl param | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `url` | Direct |
| `schema` | `extract.schema` | Direct JSON Schema passthrough |
| `prompt` | `extract.prompt` | Direct |
| `schema_mode` | — | PM-side validation; Firecrawl always uses LLM extraction |

#### webresearch → `/agent`

| PM param | Firecrawl param | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | `prompt` | Research question becomes agent prompt |
| `max_sources` | — | PM enforces post-hoc by limiting agent iterations |
| `starting_urls` | Prepended to prompt | Firecrawl agent has no explicit seed URL param |
| `timeout_ms` | `timeout` | Converted to seconds |

**Credit cost:** Firecrawl `/agent` costs 20–2500 credits per call. PM requires user confirmation when estimated cost exceeds 100 credits; hard cap default 500 credits (user-adjustable).

#### webcrawl → `/crawl`

| PM param | Firecrawl param | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `url` | Direct |
| `max_pages` | `limit` | Direct |
| `max_depth` | `maxDepth` | Direct |
| `include_paths` | `includePaths` | Direct glob patterns |
| `exclude_paths` | `excludePaths` | Direct glob patterns |
| `respect_robots` | `ignoreSitemap` (inverted) | PM default respects robots |

#### webmap → `/map`

| PM param | Firecrawl param | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `url` | Direct |
| `search` | `search` | Direct |
| `include_paths` | `includePaths` | Direct |
| `exclude_paths` | `excludePaths` | Direct |
| `use_sitemap` | `ignoreSitemap` (mapped) | `skip` → `true`, `include`/`only` → `false` |

### 10.4 Error code mapping

| Firecrawl error | PM error code | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 402 Payment Required | `credit_cap_exceeded` | Insufficient credits |
| 429 Too Many Requests | `rate_limited` | Firecrawl rate limit |
| 408 / timeout | `timeout` | Request timeout |
| 403 Forbidden | `blocked_by_robots` | Access denied by site |
| 500+ server errors | `provider_unavailable` | Firecrawl service issue |
| SSL/TLS errors | `ssl_error` | Certificate issues |
| DNS resolution failure | `dns_error` | Domain not found |

### 10.5 Firecrawl audit fields

All Firecrawl-routed web tool invocations include these additional fields in the seglog audit payload under `payload.meta`:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `firecrawl_credits_used` | `integer` | Credits consumed for this call |
| `firecrawl_cache_state` | `string` | Firecrawl-side cache status |
| `firecrawl_scrape_id` | `string` | Firecrawl request tracking ID |

### 10.6 Self-hosted limitations

Self-hosted Firecrawl instances lack Fire Engine (proprietary anti-bot technology). PM must:
- Not silently switch between self-hosted and cloud Firecrawl.
- Display provider source in activity labels (e.g., "Firecrawl (self-hosted)" vs "Firecrawl (cloud)").
- Not assume anti-bot bypass capability when routing to self-hosted instances.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

### 10.7 Interact session model (research_session)

When a web tool uses browser actions (`actions` parameter), PM creates a transient **research session** — a restricted subset of the full automation_session.

**Research session definition:**
- 15 allowed actions (of the 40 in full automation_session) organized in 3 tiers
- Ephemeral browser profile (no takeover or promotion to persistent session)
- Teardown when the parent tool invocation completes
- Escalation to full automation_session requires explicit user confirmation

**Tier 1 — Read-only (auto-allowed after host webfetch approval):**
`navigate`, `wait`, `screenshot`, `evaluate_readonly`, `scroll`, `get_text`, `get_attribute`, `get_url`, `get_title`

**Tier 2 — Light interaction (auto-allowed after "For Session" approval per GAP-11):**
`click`, `type`, `select`, `hover`, `press`, `focus`

**Tier 3 — Escalation-required (requires explicit user confirmation):**
`evaluate` (non-readonly), `file_upload`, `download`

**Lifecycle:** `created` → `active` → `complete` | `error` | `timeout`. No pause/resume — research sessions are single-shot.

**Annotation:** Every action records `{ action_type, target_selector?, timestamp_ms, screenshot_ref? }` in the seglog audit payload.

## 11. Provider capability matrix

The web tool routing system uses this matrix to determine which providers support which operations.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md, ContractName:Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md

| Provider | websearch | webfetch | webextract | webresearch | webcrawl | webmap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Exa** | `native` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| **Tavily** | `native` | `native` | `native` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| **Firecrawl** | `native` | `native` | `native` | `native` | `native` | `native` |
| **Anthropic** | `native` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| **OpenAI** | `native` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| **Google** | `native` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| **DDG** | `native` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `pm_composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |

**Capability modes:**
- `native`: Provider has a dedicated endpoint or built-in feature.
- `pm_composed`: PM orchestrates the operation using the provider's simpler primitives (e.g., search + fetch → research).
- `unsupported`: Provider cannot perform this operation even with PM composition.

**Priority order (default):** Exa > Tavily > Firecrawl > Anthropic/OpenAI > Google > DDG. Users can adjust in settings.

## 12. Web tool routing algorithm

The routing algorithm determines which provider handles a web tool invocation. It runs for every web tool call.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md

**Step 1 — Permission check:** Resolve the tool's permission key through the permission stack. If result is `deny`, stop with `permission_denied`. If `ask`, present approval card and wait.

**Step 2 — Operation identification:** Map the tool name to a canonical operation (`websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, `webmap`).

**Step 3 — Provider enumeration:** Build the ordered provider list from user settings (default: Exa > Tavily > Firecrawl > model-native > DDG). Filter to providers with `native` or `pm_composed` support for this operation.

**Step 4 — Cache check:** Compute cache key `(normalized_url, formats_hash, adapter_id)`. If cache hit and not expired per operation TTL, return cached result. Skip remaining steps.

**Step 5 — Provider health check:** For each candidate provider in priority order, check: (a) credentials configured, (b) not rate-limited, (c) endpoint reachable. Skip unhealthy providers.

**Step 6 — Capability match:** Select the first healthy provider that supports this operation. Prefer `native` over `pm_composed` when both are available at equal priority.

**Step 7 — Request dispatch:** Map PM parameters to provider-specific parameters using the mapping tables (§10.3). Dispatch the request.

**Step 8 — Fallback on failure:** If the provider returns an error, fall to the next provider in the list. Do NOT stop on first failure. Exhaust all candidates before returning error to the agent.

**Step 9 — Result normalization and audit:** Normalize the provider response to PM's canonical output format. Write the web audit payload to seglog. Update cache if applicable. Return result.

### 6.5 Four-tier approval ladder

When a tool invocation resolves to `ask`, the user is presented with an approval card offering four response tiers:

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, ContractName:Plans/Tools.md

| Tier | Label | Scope | Persistence | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deny | This invocation | Transient | Block this specific invocation. Does not create a durable rule. |
| 2 | Allow once | This invocation | Transient | Approve this specific invocation only. Next invocation re-asks. |
| 3 | For session | Current session | Session-scoped | Approve all matching invocations for the current session. Expires on session end. |
| 4 | Always | Project or global | Durable | Create a persistent rule. Offers sub-choice: project-scope or global-scope. |

**Scope modifiers for "Always":**
- **Project scope:** Rule applies only within the current project context.
- **Global scope:** Rule applies across all projects.

**Batch operations (GAP-06):** For batch web operations (batch webfetch, batch webextract), a single confirmation prompt shows all unique domains. "For Session" grants all listed domains for the session duration.

**Research session Tier 2 (GAP-11):** After the parent web tool receives "For Session" approval, Tier 2 research session actions (click, type, select, hover, press, focus) are auto-allowed without a second confirmation.

**Permission snapshots:** Permission state is snapshotted at attempt start and immutable for the duration of the attempt. Historical runs display the frozen snapshot.

**Persona profiles:** Persona profiles must NOT be mutated from in-chat approval cards (v1 policy).
